summary: Phase 0 aggregate acceptance review over the frozen six criteria. AC1-AC5 are MET on evidence executed against the current tree, including two probes written from scratch for this review: a 10-case budget probe (inclusive round ceiling, independent tool-call cap, four truthful terminal reasons, zero-valued and invalid budgets) and a scripts-typecheck probe that injects a TS2322 into two real covered scripts through an in-memory compiler-host overlay. AC6 is NOT MET: two unresolved minor evidence-quality findings (the T9 journal attributes all 27 blocking health advisories to fast-uri when they span seven packages; the full-suite 7100/18/0 result has no immutable log, only journal prose) and the AFC-16/21 remaining-scope record is task T11, which has not run. No code finding was raised: the M01 shared routing writer and the M10 budget work are correct on the tree. The health gate's fail was verified rather than accepted - all 14 P0 and 13 P1 findings are bun audit advisories on package.json, zero product-code findings at a blocking priority. Nothing under src/, scripts/ or fixtures/ has changed since the 20:11:46Z integration snapshot, so that evidence still describes the tree.

acceptance.criterion: AC3: M10 offline stub proves the actual configured round/call budget stops execution with a truthful terminal reason; maxToolCalls never silently ignored or represented by maxRounds
acceptance.evidence: T10-budget-probe.ts (written from scratch for this review, not a rerun of T16/T21 probes): 10/10 pass. maxRounds:3 -> exactly 3 provider requests and budget_exhausted; maxRounds:0 -> 0 requests; the no-progress wrap-up stays inside the ceiling (5 requests under maxRounds:6); maxToolCalls:1 with two calls in ONE round and maxRounds:10 -> 1 invocation, 1 request, 9 rounds unspent, tool_call_budget_exhausted; cap 3 across rounds -> 3 invocations, 17 rounds unspent; maxToolCalls:0 -> 0 invocations, cap not dropped; no cap -> budget never fires; a stop with 16 rounds and 47 calls left reports no_progress; maxToolCalls:-1 throws RangeError. Child side: spawn-subagent-tool.ts:841 passes maxToolCalls separately, :485 clamps max_rounds to MAX_SUBAGENT_MAX_ROUNDS=24, :1216-1218 reports both caps truthfully. Raw: .metaproject/data/gdctx/raw/2026-09-06T20-25-40-617Z_run.log

acceptance.criterion: AC6: focused regressions and integration checks have current immutable evidence; independent code-verifier/review report no unresolved blocker/major/minor findings; phase delivery accurately records remaining AFC-16/21 scope
acceptance.evidence: Three reasons, all documentation-only. (a) F-001: the T9 integration record misattributes the blocking health advisories to one package when they span seven. (b) F-002: the full-suite 7100/18/0 result has no immutable log - no gdctx raw in the 20:00-20:14Z window belongs to it, the testing artifact predates it at 15:13Z, and the health artifact's tests source is missing/not-run; the lint and typecheck halves of the same table do have immutable raws and were re-executed to exit 0. (c) T11, which owns the AFC-16/21 remaining-scope record, is pending and depends on this review. The findings half is otherwise clean: T15 0/0/0, T21 0 findings, T16-final's 1 major + 3 minor verified closed on the tree, and both T9 blockers verified fixed (http-sse.ts:67 no longer trusts the configured DNS host; health/gate.ts:68-81 escalates a skipped required source to incomplete, pinned by health-truthful-gate.test.ts:117).

artifacts.summary: Aggregate acceptance review: per-criterion verdicts with executed evidence, 3 findings, acceptance recommendation, stale-evidence section, routing audit.

AC3 probe written from scratch: 10 hard-asserted cases over the inclusive round ceiling, the independent tool-call cap and the four terminal reasons. Deterministic in-memory provider, no network, no working-tree writes.
AC5 probe: injects a TS2322 into two real covered scripts through an in-memory TypeScript compiler-host overlay and asserts the diagnostic is attributed to those files. Read-only on the repository.

findings.problem: The 2026-09-06T20:12:54Z integration record states that all 14 P0 health findings are dependency advisories on the transitive package fast-uri, with 13 P1 and 1 P2 from the same source. The counts match the artifact but the attribution does not: the 27 blocking-priority findings span seven packages (fast-uri 6xP0, protobufjs 6xP0+5xP1, sharp 1xP0, ip-address 1xP0+2xP1, hono 3xP1, @hono/node-server 1xP1, qs 2xP1), and the single P2 dependency advisory is hono, not fast-uri.
findings.impact: The record builds a phase-8 prioritisation argument on the fast-uri attribution, so a reader scoping the dependency refresh from it would plan for one package and meet seven, with six of the fourteen P0 advisories in a package the record never names. The material claim the acceptance rests on is unaffected: every blocking finding is source dependencyAudit on package.json and the count of blocking-priority product-code findings is 0, independently verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Append a journal correction naming the seven packages and their per-priority counts, and carry the corrected inventory into the T11 delivery record and the phase-8 hand-off. No code change.

findings.problem: AC6 requires current immutable evidence for the integration checks, and this flow's context.md:13 required immutable per-worker report paths, but the full-suite result (7100 pass / 18 skip / 0 fail, 54038 assertions, 7118 tests in 579 files, 199s) exists only as prose in the journal. No gdctx raw log in the 20:00-20:14Z window belongs to it (all five are flow 233 T76 output), .metaproject/data/testing/artifacts/latest.json predates the run at 15:13Z, the health artifact's own tests source is status missing / execution not-run, and T9 attempt 3 wrote no result artifact (T9-result.json is attempt 1/2 from 15:33Z).
findings.impact: The most load-bearing claim in the phase is the one an auditor cannot check, in a phase whose own history records three cases of an implementer's artifact claim being false while the returned value was right. The lint and typecheck halves of the same table do have immutable raws (.metaproject/data/health/raw/{eslint,typescript}/2026-09-06T20-11-30-148Z.log) and were re-executed to exit 0 during this review, so the gap is specific to the suite figure.
findings.suggested_fix: Rerun the full suite once through keryx ctx run (or keryx test) so an immutable raw log exists, and cite that path beside the numbers in the journal and in T11; or, if no rerun is wanted before delivery, have T11 state plainly that the suite figure rests on an unlogged run. No code change.
